provenance.quote: Shall the City and County of Broomfield lodging taxes be increased up to $3,300,000.00 annually in 2027, the first full fiscal year of collection, and by whatever amount is raised annually thereafter, by increasing the lodging tax rate by four point four percent (4.4%) for a total rate of six percent (6%) on the rental fee, price, or other consideration paid or charged for the short-term rental (less than 30 consecutive days) of any room, accommodation, or space in any hotel, inn, bed and breakfast residence, or any other place that provides sleeping rooms, sleeping facilities, or accommodations for consideration located within the City and County of Broomfield, commencing on January 1, 2027, with the revenues of such lodging tax to be dedicated for use by the housing authority of the City and County of Broomfield to preserve and expand housing opportunities in Broomfield, the housing authority being governed by a board appointed by the City Council and required to provide annual expenditures reports to the City Council, and shall all revenues from such taxes and any earnings thereon be collected, retained, and spent as a voter-approved revenue change without limitation or condition, and notwithstanding any revenue or expenditure limitations contained in Article X Section 20 of the Colorado Constitution or any other law?
provenance.sourceOrg: City and County of Broomfield Attorney’s Office

measures.officialStatement:
Ballot Question 1B proposes a new 20-year franchise agreement with Public Service
Company of Colorado (“Xcel Energy”), commencing on January 1, 2028. Xcel has a
current franchise agreement with CCOB, approved by the voters in 2007, that will
expire December 31, 2027.
The franchise agreement, attached to Ordinance 2307, sets forth the specific terms,
fees, compensation, and other conditions of a gas and electric franchise agreement
with Xcel Energy. It grants the non-exclusive right to use public rights-of-way and
property to install, maintain, and repair infrastructure necessary to provide gas and
electric service. Under the proposed agreement, the franchise fee (3%) and
undergrounding fund contributions (1%) paid by Xcel Energy to CCOB remain identical
to those in the current agreement.
The franchise agreement does not set utility rates, and it does not govern Xcel
Energy’s plans, designs, or builds of utility infrastructure.

measures.questionText: Shall Section 4.3 of the Broomfield Home Rule Charter be amended so future mayors will serve a 4-year term and be limited to two consecutive terms starting at the general municipal election to be held in 2027?
measures.officialStatement:
Ballot Question 1C proposes amending Section 4.3 of the Broomfield Home Rule
Charter to change the mayoral term of office from a 2-year term to a 4-year term,
while also changing the term limits from three consecutive terms to two consecutive
terms. If approved, this change would go into effect with the 2027 mayoral election.
It would not impact the current mayor’s term of office or term limits.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Raise Broomfield’s lodging tax from 1.6% to 6%, starting January 1, 2027, for paid stays of less than 30 consecutive days. It would raise up to $3.3 million in 2027 and amounts based on collections annually afterward. All lodging-tax revenue would be dedicated to Broomfield’s housing authority to preserve and expand housing opportunities. Its council-appointed board would report spending to the council annually. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue and spending limits and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the lodging-tax increase, dedicated housing revenue and revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Approve a new 20-year gas and electric franchise agreement with Xcel Energy beginning January 1, 2028, after the current agreement expires December 31, 2027. It would grant nonexclusive use of public streets and property for utility infrastructure, continue moving overhead electrical lines underground, address infrastructure safety and emergency coordination, and require payments to Broomfield. The existing 3% franchise fee and 1% undergrounding contribution would stay the same. The agreement would not set utility rates.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the 20-year franchise agreement and its payments and programs.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject the proposed franchise agreement; the attorney’s booklet says Xcel would continue providing service under state utility rules.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Change future Broomfield mayoral terms from 2 years to 4 years and change the limit from 3 consecutive terms to 2 consecutive terms. The change would begin with the 2027 municipal election and would not affect the current mayor’s term or term limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve four-year mayoral terms with a two-consecutive-term limit starting in 2027.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep two-year mayoral terms and the three-consecutive-term limit.
